chunks: And in the narration of Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, he said:

"The waiting period of the woman who undergoes khulʿ is the waiting period of the divorced woman. Her khulʿ is her divorce, and it suffices without explicitly naming it as divorce. And the woman seeking khulʿ, her khulʿ is not lawful until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not keep any oath to you, nor obey any command of yours, nor perform ghusl for you from janabah, and I will surely let another tread upon your bed, and I will surely admit against you without your permission.' People in his presence had been allowing less than this. So when the woman says that to her husband, what he takes from her becomes lawful for him, and she remains before him with two remaining divorce counts, and khulʿ is one divorce."
And he عليه السلام said: "The statement should come from her own side." Meaning: without her being taught.

key_terms.الْكَلَامُ: the statement or declaration that must come from the woman herself
key_terms.الْمُخْتَلِعَةِ: a woman who seeks separation through khulʿ
key_terms.تَطْلِيقَتَيْنِ: two remaining divorce counts after the khulʿ
key_terms.جَنَابَةٍ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.خُلْعُهَا: her khulʿ separation in return for compensation
key_terms.طَلَاقُهَا: her divorce, meaning khulʿ counts legally as divorce
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: the waiting period legally observed after separation

ai.seo_question: What are the legal conditions and effects of khulʿ according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings for khulʿ, stating that its ʿiddah is the same as that of divorce and that khulʿ itself counts as one divorce. It also specifies that khulʿ is only valid when the woman herself expresses severe aversion and unwillingness to continue the marital relationship, without being coached to say so.
